newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CECIL FIELDER, WIFE TO SEEK $25 MILLION IN SUIT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CECIL FIELDER, WIFE TO SEEK $25 MILLION IN SUIT.

text.p: New York Yankees' first baseman and designated hitter Cecil Fielder and his wife Stacey said Wednesday they would file a $25 million lawsuit against a Florida sheriff's office alleging Stacey Fielder was arrested falsely last month.

The Fielders stood behind their attorney, Willie Gary, at a news conference as Gary detailed the incident early last month in which Stacey Fielder, 31, was handcuffed, arrested and detained at a holding station by the Brevard County Sheriff's deputies.
Gary said Stacey Fielder's arrest -- she was charged with resisting arrest without violence -- and the way she was treated appeared racially motivated.
"We won't stand for it," said Gary, a prominent civil attorney who is the Rev. Jesse Jackson's personal lawyer.

The incident occured near Melbourne, Florida, when Stacey Fielder was returning home from a charity fund-raiser she had sponsored with her husband. She stopped at an accident and realised her 10-year-old son and a nephew were involved, Gary said.

The other driver involved in the accident, who was white, was yelling obscenities at her nephew but was not admonished by the deputy at the scene, Gary said. Instead the deputy turned on Mrs. Fielder when she asked him about her son's condition, he said.

"He didn't even want her to inquire about her child ... he told her she should just leave," Gary said. Stacey Fielder persisted, he said, and was taken away for several hours to a holding station, given an embarrassing body search and then released with a notice to appear in court.
"Cecil said enough is enough and now it's time for us to stand up for what we believe in," Gary said. "At this point, we just feel it's war now. Flat out war."
Brevard Sheriff's spokeswoman Joan Heller said the allegation that Stacey Fielder was treated differently because of her race was "categorically untrue."
